hints.title: Ten-Second Message Throttling
hints.text: Duplicate messages must be suppressed if fewer than ten seconds elapsed since their last approved display timestamp.

hints.title: Timestamp Lookup and Update
hints.text: Record the timestamp of each displayed message in a dictionary. When a message arrives, check whether timestamp is at least previous timestamp plus ten.

hints.title: Rate Limiter Decision Blueprint
hints.text: If message in self.history and timestamp < self.history[message] + 10, return false. Otherwise, update self.history[message] = timestamp and return true.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.space: O(M) where M is unique messages observed
variables: M: count of distinct log message strings
complexity.notes: Direct hash map lookup and insertion per incoming event.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning linear log buffers over time windows introduces unbounded latency as message volume expands.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Retaining the latest approval timestamp per string enables O(1) rate checks.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct boundary comparison (timestamp < history + 10 suppresses, >= 10 allows).

solutions.approach: C++ Hash Map Log Rate Limiter
